Do you compensate for a long delay?

Sent · Just now

ByRo Bot · AI

ByRo Bot · AI says:

We do offer forms of compensation when there’s a long delay, but it depends on the situation:

Rental arrives late to the renter:

You’re generally entitled to a full refund if the item is late and you return it within 24 hours of delivery.
If you return it after 24 hours, you may receive a partial refund, based on how many days of the rental were effectively lost.
If you keep the item beyond the original rental period, you can still be liable for late fees, even if it arrived late.

Item delayed in the mail by courier:

The sender must contact the courier to investigate.
If a paid guaranteed/next-day service wasn’t met, the sender may be able to claim a refund or compensation directly from the courier.

Late return delays:

If an item is returned late (because the renter posted it late), late fees can be charged, but they’re capped and meant to cover missed bookings rather than be punitive.
If the renter posted on time and only the postal system caused the delay, late fees can’t be charged as long as tracked proof shows it was sent on or before the final rental day.

So yes, there are refund/fee protections in place for long delays, both for items arriving late to renters and for courier failures, as long as each party follows the posting and reporting rules.
